record.provider: JFrog Artifactory Cloud — free tier (historically 2 GB)

free_tier.stated: 2 GB total storage + 10 GB/month data transfer on the legacy 'JFrog Free' cloud subscription. That tier is no longer generally available: JFrog's own blog now carries the banner 'The below post showcases the JFrog Platform Free Tier, which is currently limited for new sign-ups.' The live pricing page has no free tier at all. The entry point is Pro at $50/mo with 25 GB base consumption.

retention.stated: 2 GB total storage (not per month. A Stack Overflow answer from a JFrog employee confirms it is total, and you must delete to reclaim); 10 GB/month transfer; 2,000 build minutes; 21-day inactivity deactivation.

egress.terms: 10 GB/month included on the legacy free tier; beyond that the platform bills 'Consumption = Storage + Transfer' against the included base. Not free, not Cloudflare-coverable.

record.interface_detail: rest (Artifactory REST), JFrog CLI, native package clients, OCI
record.tooling: JFrog CLI, `curl -T`, `docker push`, `twine upload`. Best-in-class tooling, which is why the 2 GB cap is such a shame.
record.chaining: Previously: one free cloud instance per account, × unlimited accounts, at 2 GB each. Now gated: 'limited for new sign-ups', and accounts are deactivated after '21 days with no data transfer activity'. So a dormant bulk store dies.
record.limits_note: 2 GB total storage (not per month. A Stack Overflow answer from a JFrog employee confirms it is total, and you must delete to reclaim); 10 GB/month transfer; 2,000 build minutes; 21-day inactivity deactivation.
record.reliability_note: Repeated policy churn (free tier gated, then 2 GB → 25 GB Pro) plus inactivity deactivation makes it unsafe as storage.

evidence.proved: read live: 'currently limited for new sign-ups'; 'The subscription is generous with 10GB of data transfer per month, 2,000 build minutes per month and 2GB total storage'; 'accounts that experience 21 days with no data transfer activity will be deactivated'
read live 2026-10-21: plan ladder is Pro 25 GB base / Enterprise 125 GB base; no free row anywhere, entry price $50/month
read live: 'The Cloud version includes 2GB of peak data storage, 10GB of monthly data transfer'

record.provider: JFrog Artifactory Community Edition (CE for C/C++) / Artifactory OSS — self-hosted

free_tier.stated: Free of charge, self-hosted, no storage cap of any kind: the quota is whatever disk/object-store you attach. 'This product gives all the power and flexibility of the Artifactory repository for Conan and generic binaries to the C/C++ world completely free of charge.' OSS edition likewise downloadable and free.

egress.terms: Free by construction. You serve it from your own host/object store, so egress is your bill (or zero behind Cloudflare). Not a hosted egress concession.

record.interface_detail: rest (Artifactory REST API), plus every native protocol it supports: docker/OCI, maven, npm, pypi, nuget, generic, conan; JFrog CLI
record.tooling: JFrog CLI (`jf rt upload`), `curl -T` against the REST API, `oras`/`docker push` for OCI, and any package client. Real, first-party, actively maintained.
record.chaining: Not really chainable as free storage: each instance consumes your own disk. The only 'multiplier' is running it on someone else's free compute/disk, which is a different niche (IaaS), not an artifact-manager finding.
record.limits_note: CE for C/C++ is restricted to Conan + generic repository types only (no Docker/Maven/npm); OSS edition likewise feature-stripped. No HA, no S3 blob store on CE. Requires you to run Java + Postgres/derby and to pay for the bytes.
record.reliability_note: Mature, no data-vanishing risk; the catch is that 'free' means free software, not free storage. You are the storage provider.

evidence.proved: read live: 'completely free of charge to any software team'; 'containing support only for Conan and generic repositories'

read live: 'It is completely free, and features a WebUI, advanced authentication and permissions ... a REST API, a generic CLI tool and generic repositories to host any kind of source or binary artifact'
read live: live download links for OSS (tar.gz, rpm, deb, docker, helm) — the free edition is still shipping
